oracle: Literal finite battery states (v,e),0<=e<=N; chargers reset immediately to N, noncharger energy0 dies before attempting the next edge. A state loses if every next state loses at an A-owned vertex, or any next state loses at a B-owned vertex. A synchronous finite safety fixed point is computed on the expanded graph. This uses neither repeated Buchi-region elimination, SCC cycle certificates, nor first-visit/fixed-policy enumeration. Run unrestricted, then with just returned A moves fixed, then just returned B moves fixed; both opponents remain adaptive and may depend on remaining energy.
sourceVsExpandedProof: The independently reviewed positional A strategy has no reachable target-free cycle even against adaptive B, so any charge gap is <=N. The independently reviewed positional B strategy forces only finitely many charges even against adaptive A, and thus eventually battery exhaustion. Therefore the capacity-N finite safety classifications must equal the original first-visit source classifications. The independent oracle also explicitly distinguishes capacity N from N-1 on every single-charger N-cycle for N=2..64.
memoryScope: Live requested allocation payload only, excluding allocator/header/ASan overhead, caller preexisting arguments, compiler, oracle graphs. Only API-created storage is allocated in the measurement window; expected answers are constructed beforehand. Only the tested N5000/M20000/2500-deletion-round construction is measured, not a universal maximum-byte claim.
